name: Phu Quoc fish sauce
summary: Anchovy fish sauce aged in wooden vats, dark as a cockroach wing, salty and deeply sweet with a natural fat. It smells light and clean, with no fishy or ammonia edge.
origin: Phu Quoc. Hội nước mắm Phú Quốc dates a geographical indication to 2001 and European protection to 8 October 2012. Fermenting and bottling stay inside the old huyện Phú Quốc.
history: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the craft is over 200 years old, with about 20 family houses in the 1950s by the Dương Đông river. The 3-day account also says over 200 years, and calls the island the country’s leading producer. About 100 producers are on the tourism account. Decision 1307 of 16 June 2017 was announced 18 August 2017.
culture: The association keeps anchovy at least 85 percent. The salt ratio is 2.5–3 fish to 1 salt, and 12 months, on the association account. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says 3 tons of fish to 1 ton of salt, about one year, and one cá cơm than workshop at 15 months and 43 percent. Vats are 3 m across and hold 14–17 tons. The catch on that account runs April–November. That is the fishery, not a shop hour.
taste: Hội nước mắm Phú Quốc: dark cockroach-wing colour, a light aroma without a fishy or ammonia smell, salty and deeply sweet, with a natural fat. Nitrogen 20–43 gN/lít, and up to 40°N in the introduction. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the pure sauce is dark brown, clear, and thick, salty, gently sweet, and fragrant of cá cơm sọc tiêu, and the district account says sweet and fragrant, trên 25ºC. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism, writing about fish sauce in the country, says the taste can be briny and rounded, with sweetness, a mineral note, or caramel, and that it should smell strong but not stinky. The association places the catch in the Gulf of Thailand, Kiên Giang and Cà Mau waters. That country account says the clear Andaman Sea. Every figure stays.
howToEat: Taste it at a barrel house. Across Vietnam, a diluted sauce with vinegar and water goes with fried spring rolls, a teaspoon with chili and garlic goes into fishy soups, pure sauce goes with steamed vegetables, and a blend with sugar and lime goes with fresh rolls.
where: The barrel houses, historically along the Dương Đông river.
seoTitle: Nuoc mam Phu Quoc — anchovy fish sauce
seoDescription: Nước mắm Phú Quốc is anchovy sauce aged in wooden vats: dark, salty, deeply sweet, and clean-smelling. Taste it at a barrel house.
